lastCompletedStory.title: Backstop produces a handoff: signal the agent, then deterministic minimal fallback, then respawn

nextStoryContext: checkBackstop (src/commands/orch-recycle-watch.ts) now runs the full signal-then-fallback episode state machine on top of US-001's handoff-exists guard: over-threshold + no handoff yet + no signal outstanding signals the orchestrator pane once (BACKSTOP_SIGNAL_TEXT via sendKeysWhenIdle, atomic send-keys, no -l) and stamps episode.signaledAt (nowFn()); repeated polls within signalTimeoutMs (default 30s, DEFAULT_SIGNAL_TIMEOUT_MS) no-op; once the grace period elapses with still no handoff, writeMinimalHandoffFn() (production: makeWriteMinimalHandoffFn -> writeOrchHandoff + buildMinimalBackstopHandoff, first PRODUCTION caller of writeOrchHandoff from src/orchestrator/handoff.ts) writes a deterministic handoff (schemaVersion 1, reason 'context-backstop', pointers: prdPath, gitBranch, loopFile, journalTail) then arms the marker. All seams (tmuxSpawnFn, resolveOrchPaneIdFn, signalPaneFn, writeMinimalHandoffFn, nowFn, signalTimeoutMs) are injectable on OrchRecycleWatchOptions/BackstopDeps; BackstopEpisodeState.signaledAt is the sole mutable per-episode field, allocated once per watcher lifetime. AC6 (buildOrchestratorPaneCommand in src/commands/run.ts takes the respawn branch, never kill-session, for a context-backstop handoff) needed NO src/commands/run.ts code change: a new test/commands/run.test.ts proves the existing bash wrapper logic (handoff present + reason != cycle-close increments the respawn counter) already holds for reason 'context-backstop' by running the real assembled script with only the `claude` invocation stubbed out. file-size-budget.json _ref raised for src/orchestrator/handoff.ts (107->148, buildMinimalBackstopHandoff + MinimalBackstopHandoffPointers). No remaining stories reference CAM-172 in prd.json as of this write; check prd.json for what follows.

officialDocsValidated.summary: Confirmed send-keys -l forces literal-character mode (so 'Enter' would be sent as 4 literal chars, never submitting); the implementation's atomic signalPaneFn/sendKeysWhenIdle call never passes -l, so 'Enter' resolves as the named key and the text+Enter submit in one call, matching the sendkeys-literal-enter-gotcha invariant.
